pll1d10c1-d1e3477.summary: Turns, after the Son's eternity, to the Holy Spirit and states the thesis that the Spirit is the love, charity, or dilection of the Father and Son.
claims: The Holy Spirit is the love of the Father and the Son.

pll1d10c1-d1e3489.summary: With De Trinitate XV, the Spirit belongs to both and suggests their common charity. Since John says 'God is charity,' not 'the Spirit is charity,' it is uncertain whether Father, Son, Spirit, or the Trinity is meant.
claims: The Holy Spirit belongs to both Father and Son.
The Spirit indicates the common charity of Father and Son.
'God is charity' does not by itself specify which person is meant.

pll1d10c1-d1e3537.summary: Gives Augustine's answer: Father, Son, and Spirit are each wisdom and together one wisdom, and likewise charity. Yet as the Word is properly called wisdom, the Spirit is most aptly called charity properly, since in the simple nature substance is charity and charity substance in each person.
claims: Charity is said of each person and of all three as one charity.
The Holy Spirit is most aptly called charity in a proper sense.
In God substance and charity are identical.

pll1d10c1-d1e3564.summary: Draws the lesson: in the Trinity 'charity' sometimes refers to the substance common to and whole in each person, sometimes specially to the Spirit, as 'wisdom' sometimes means the divine substance and sometimes properly the Son.
claims: 'Charity' sometimes signifies the divine substance, sometimes the Holy Spirit.
Likewise 'wisdom' sometimes signifies the substance, sometimes the Son.

pl-l1d10c1.summary: Begins the treatment of the Holy Spirit: the Spirit is the love or charity of the Father and Son. With Augustine, the Spirit belongs to both and suggests the common charity by which they love each other. Since 1 John says 'God is charity,' not 'the Holy Spirit is charity,' one must ask which is meant. Augustine answers that, as wisdom is said of each and all, so is charity, yet charity is properly said of the Spirit, just as wisdom is properly said of the Son. So charity sometimes names the common substance and sometimes properly the Spirit.
claims: The Holy Spirit is the love or charity of the Father and the Son.
The Spirit is common to Father and Son and indicates the charity by which they love each other.
Charity is said of each person and of all three as one charity, as wisdom is.
Charity is properly attributed to the Holy Spirit, as wisdom is to the Son.
In God substance and charity are the same.
concepts: mutual love of Father and Son
